assessments.statement: Task update and journal types are Task-owned; in-memory-team-port.ts keeps compatibility type re-exports without becoming their authority.
Task delivery consumes an injected TaskReconciliationQuery and no longer imports Beads Task adapters dynamically; the static production file graph remains acyclic.

Task mutation orchestration depends on a consumer-owned publication port. A stateless durable adapter outside Task authority owns concrete Coordination, failed-hint, and Task-delivery calls, and Pi composition injects one publishing factory into leader and Worker mutation paths.
ModelToolTeamPort, DurableModelToolTeamPort, and the in-memory implementation combine all five semantic boundaries plus rc.10 liveness and sync-nudge behavior in one seam.

The rc.10 tree implements page-safe hydration, liveness, failed-event hints, bounded waits, indeterminate outcomes, and branch-bound nudges, but Coordination still reads Team runtime, Task delivery, and Alert inbox records concretely and remains split across the facade and Pi composition.

Worker carrier realization consumes the Team-owned TeamLifecyclePublication port. The durable adapter stays outside Team authority, calls existing Coordination/runtime operations, and the former utils module is a compatibility re-export. This isolates carrier publication and bounded startup observation only.
TeamConfig and models.ts preserve required current compatibility but mix facts from more than one authority.
Membership observation remains additive and core-independent, but broad private record imports increase compatibility coupling.

risks.statement: Moving code can change lock, commit, event, delivery, acknowledgement, or hook order even when public schemas remain stable.
One in-memory store can make cross-authority atomicity appear stronger than the durable implementation.
Splitting mixed contracts can reject or rewrite supported historical Team, Task, event, inbox, terminal, and delivery records.
Changing private Team or runtime records can change the additive public Membership projection unless decoding is isolated.
WorkerRunObservation can become a competing authority if direct runtime, Task-delivery, or Alert-inbox reads are treated as work truth instead of bounded actuation evidence.

Failed-event hints, timers, reservations, and presented sync-nudge receipts are derived coordination evidence; they must not mutate or replace Team, Task, Alert, or acknowledged observation authority.

dependencyRules: Pi composition root depends on trio-facing registration and projections.
The trio-facing facade depends on separate Team, Task, Alert, and Coordination application ports.
Coordination depends on read-only Team, Task, and Alert query ports.
Task and Alert each own their current-Membership resolver interface; composition-root adapters implement it by calling a Team query port.
Team owns its assigned-work guard interface; a composition-root adapter implements it by calling a Task query port.
Consumer-owned cross-authority ports create runtime collaboration, not direct authority source dependencies.
Membership observation depends only on a narrow read-only Team/runtime projection.
No authority imports trio-facing schemas, renderers, test doubles, or another authority to implement a reverse query.
